smell: Provider.Provision and Provider.retrieveProvisionResult still raise bare fmt.Errorf for config-class / cluster-runtime failures ('no VMs provisioned; check config', 'static IP start address is required for OKD deployments'). The prior sweep fixed Connect (line 85, 88 now use ConfigError); these two adjacent sites were missed. At cli/root.go:exitCodeFor both hit the default branch and exit 1 instead of 2 (ConfigError) or 4 (ClusterError).
severity_reason: Breaks the cli/root.go:145 exit-code contract documented in errtypes.go:1-4 and cli/root.go:1-7, but on a low-traffic path. Recurring from prior run; the prior sweep caught the Connect() path but these adjacent sites were missed.
fix_summary: Line 182: wrap with &errtypes.ClusterError{Msg: "terraform apply succeeded but no VMs were provisioned; check config"} (cluster-runtime failure, exit 4). Line 237: wrap with &errtypes.ConfigError{Msg: "static IP start address is required for OKD deployments"} (config, exit 2).
rule_source: counter-example: internal/infrastructure/proxmox/proxmox.go:85-88 (Connect uses ConfigError correctly after prior sweep)
must_preserve: exit-code taxonomy documented in cli/root.go:1-7. Do not introduce new exit codes here — cli-ux owns the taxonomy.

smell: Four sites still use `if err != nil || !X.Is4()` and return a synthetic fmt.Errorf that drops the netip.ParseAddr / netip.ParsePrefix error entirely. Debugging 'invalid IPv4 address: 192.168' gives no hint whether netip rejected the format, the IP-version check rejected it, or a whitespace issue. Sibling sites in the same file (lines 18, 40, 119, 124, 134) correctly wrap with %w.
severity_reason: Low cost of keeping; purely diagnostic. Validation errors are user-facing strings — the synthetic message is arguably more readable than 'ParseAddr("192.168"): no suffix'. Recurring from prior run.
fix_summary: Split the conditional so parse-err and is4-check produce different messages, or wrap on the err-present case: `if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("invalid IPv4 address %q: %w", startIP, err) } if !addr.Is4() { return fmt.Errorf("IPv6 not supported: %q", startIP) }`. Matches the 'invalid CIDR %q: %w' pattern at internal/netutil/ip.go:18.
rule_source: counter-example: internal/netutil/ip.go:18,40,119,124,134 (same file wraps other parse errors with %w)
must_preserve: Validation message readability — don't replace the user-facing text with the raw netip error unconditionally.

smell: execute() still checks `if ctx.Err() != nil` to decide whether to return 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM). This works today because the hand-rolled signal handler always cancels the ctx before ExecuteContext returns, but it's fragile: a future subcommand that returns context.Canceled WITHOUT the parent ctx being canceled hits exitCodeFor instead of the 130/143 branch. The robust form is `if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` on the returned err.
severity_reason: Current code is correct under the signal-handling contract at root.go:82-105 — no user-visible bug. The robustness gap is latent. The atomic.Value for signal discrimination (landed in task-16-B4) depends on the ctx-canceled side-channel; both must coordinate for correctness.
fix_summary: Change to `if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) { /* ... SIGTERM/SIGINT branch ... */ }`. Keeps the 130/143 semantic but matches the err chain directly instead of the outer ctx state. Phase code already %w-chains ctx.Err() everywhere after prior sweeps (monitor.go/exec.go now correct).
rule_source: Go stdlib errors.Is docs: 'An error is considered to match a target if it is equal to that target or if it implements a method Is(error) bool'

smell: ErrNotConnected and ErrTerraformNotConfigured are package-level sentinels defined outside errtypes. Still never matched with errors.Is anywhere in the repo — callers only propagate them as-is. Provisioner-state failures ('not connected', 'terraform not configured') are ConfigError-semantic (programming/config bugs, exit code 2). Recurring from prior run; logged in roadmap as scaffolding per MEMORY.md §7.
severity_reason: ad-hoc exported sentinel with no errors.Is callers. Fits MEMORY.md §scaffolding — they pair with a hypothetical Connected() probe or a future errors.Is discriminator. Downgraded to suggestion per §7.
fix_summary: Either (a) lift to errtypes as ConfigError constructors or (b) keep and document 'these are matching sentinels for errors.Is — callers SHOULD match, not string-sniff'. Option (b) preserves the 'provider violated its lifecycle' semantic, which ConfigError would blur. Recommend: revisit if a second caller appears that would match.
must_preserve: Exported sentinel surface — removing breaks any future caller wanting to errors.Is against them.

smell: errtypes vocabulary covers Config/Network/Cluster/Auth but still has NO typed error for two concepts the phases hit repeatedly: (a) 'recoverable — retry or re-run' (used ad-hoc across addon/manager.go, install/flux.go as generic wrapped errors), and (b) 'cert-pending / CSR-not-yet-approved' (install/monitor.go:111-113 still logs CSR errors as Warn with no type). Recurring from prior run; logged in roadmap as scaffolding gap.
severity_reason: Scaffolding / vocabulary gap — adding types requires no caller change, only gives new callers a surface. MEMORY.md §scaffolding applies: these are symmetric-API parallels to the existing four types.
fix_summary: Add `type RecoverableError struct { Msg string; Err error; Hint string }` and `type CertPendingError struct { NodeName string; CSRName string }` with standard Error()/Unwrap() methods. Extend cli/root.go:exitCodeFor to map Recoverable→75 (EX_TEMPFAIL per sysexits) and CertPending→4 (existing ClusterError code). Only emit when a concrete caller adopts them; otherwise this stays scaffolding.
must_preserve: Existing ConfigError/NetworkError/ClusterError/AuthError — do not rename; only add new types.

smell: executor.ExitError doc still claims 'errors.Is to compare against Unwrap chain values' but the type has no Unwrap() method and no Err field. The claim is aspirational — there is nothing in the chain to traverse. terraform.ExecError is now an alias to this type (terraform.go:26) so the drift has spread by reference. Either add an Err field and Unwrap() (to carry *exec.ExitError from the underlying cmd.Run) or correct the comment.
severity_reason: No user-visible bug; comment vs code drift. Suggestion because the fix (add Err + Unwrap) does enable errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) on a ctx-killed subprocess — but no current caller needs it. Cleaner to correct the comment than grow the type.
fix_summary: Option A (recommended, -1 LOC): remove 'errors.Is to compare against Unwrap chain values' from the doc comment — the type doesn't currently chain. Option B (+5 LOC): add `Err error` field, populate from executor.run's `err` var when cmd.Run fails, implement Unwrap(). Terraform.ExecError already aliases to this type so no duplication needed. Prefer Option A unless a concrete caller needs ctx-identity propagation.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'Don't just check errors, handle them gracefully'
must_preserve: Existing ExitError.Error() message format (callers log it).

smell: Flux.Install returns a bare fmt.Errorf('helm is required to install Flux') when helm is missing. The message is user-friendly but the error carries no chain or type — it's a tool-prerequisite failure that semantically matches ConfigError (missing external dep is a configuration/environment issue, exit 2). Same pattern recurs at flux.go:148 'flux repository not configured', :332 'flux repository not configured', :391 'empty repository URL'. …
severity_reason: Outer wrap at addon/manager.go:120 preserves ClusterError exit-code 4 already — but semantically 'helm missing' should be ConfigError (exit 2). Low user impact since exit-code-4 is still surfaced; consistency drift.
fix_summary: For tool-prerequisite errors (line 72) and config errors (:148, :332, :391), wrap with &errtypes.ConfigError{Msg: ...} so the underlying chain carries correct classification. addon/manager.go:installAndVerify should then errors.As for ConfigError before wrapping as ClusterError, preserving the 'tool missing' vs 'install failed' distinction at the outer boundary.
must_preserve: User-facing message text — do not downgrade readability. Outer ClusterError wrap at addon/manager.go:120 stays (exit code 4 mapping).

smell: InstallAll aggregates failures via errors.Join(errs...) after wrapping each with ClusterError at installAndVerify:120. Good pattern. BUT the aggregated err returned to the caller has no ctx-cancellation preservation: if ctx is canceled mid-loop, ctx.Err() is returned early at line 86, but if cancellation races with a genuine install failure, the failure wins and the joined error lacks a cancellation sentinel. errors.Is(aggregated, context.Canceled) may return false even if cancellation was the trigger. Minor because the early-check at line 85-87 catches most cases.
severity_reason: Cancellation-identity is preserved when ctx.Err() fires between addons (line 85-87). Only the race window between 'installAndVerify started' and 'ctx.Err check next iteration' is exposed. Latent; no current symptom.
fix_summary: After the for-loop, add `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil && len(errs) > 0 { errs = append(errs, err) }` so the joined error includes the ctx sentinel when cancellation contributed. Alternatively, make installAndVerify itself wrap ctx.Err via %w when Install/Verify return a ctx-related error.
rule_source: Go stdlib: errors.Join preserves individual matching — adding context.Canceled to the joined error makes errors.Is pass
must_preserve: ClusterError wrapping at manager.go:120 (exit-code 4 mapping preserved).
